backlog.title: Order backlog
backlog.content:
Backlog is confirmed, unfulfilled customer orders -- a leading indicator that runs ahead of recognised revenue by roughly one to two quarters.

For TE Connectivity: backlog is reported for both segments; a segment's backlog growing faster than its booked revenue signals accelerating demand (or longer lead times) that has not yet shown up in the P&L.

What to watch:

  • Backlog growth versus trailing revenue growth, by segment
  • Book-to-bill below 1x (backlog shrinking) as an early warning before revenue turns

geography.title: Revenue by geography
geography.content:
Revenue split across TE Connectivity's three reporting regions: Europe/Middle East/Africa, the Americas and Asia-Pacific.

For TE Connectivity: APAC is the largest region and the one most exposed to the automotive and electronics supply chain in China and Southeast Asia, so it carries more cyclicality than the Americas or EMEA.

What to watch:

  • APAC growth diverging from the other two regions (global auto production cycles)
  • Currency translation effects embedded in regional totals (reported, not organic)

industrialEndMarkets.title: Industrial Solutions by end-market
industrialEndMarkets.content:
The five end-markets that make up the Industrial Solutions segment: Digital Data Networks (AI/data-centre connectivity), Automation & Connected Living, Energy (grid and renewables), Aerospace, Defense & Marine, and Medical.

For TE Connectivity: Digital Data Networks is the AI-datacentre growth story inside an otherwise mature industrial mix -- it has grown fastest of the five and is the segment's main re-rating argument.

What to watch:

  • Digital Data Networks' share of segment revenue rising
  • Medical, the smallest and most cyclical of the five, as a swing factor

organicGrowthSegment.title: Organic growth by segment
organicGrowthSegment.content:
Organic growth strips out the effect of acquisitions, divestitures and currency translation, isolating demand for the existing business. Shown here for the total company and for each of the two segments.

For TE Connectivity: Industrial Solutions (AI datacentre and industrial automation exposure) has run well ahead of Transportation Solutions (tied to global auto production) in recent periods -- the gap is the segment-mix story behind the headline growth number.

What to watch:

  • A widening gap between the two segments' organic growth
  • Reported growth (not shown here) diverging from organic growth -- the difference is FX and M&A

segmentMargin.title: Segment operating margin
segmentMargin.content:
Segment operating income divided by segment revenue -- each segment's own profitability, before corporate overhead allocation.

For TE Connectivity: Transportation Solutions has historically carried the higher margin of the two on automotive-connector scale economics; a narrowing gap, or Industrial Solutions overtaking it, would mark a real mix shift as Digital Data Networks grows.

What to watch:

  • Margin trend by segment, not just the blended OperatingMargin chart above
  • Which segment is driving a change in the consolidated margin

segmentRevenue.title: Revenue by segment
segmentRevenue.content:
TE Connectivity reports two segments: Transportation Solutions (automotive, commercial transportation and sensors connectors) and Industrial Solutions (industrial equipment, aerospace/defense/marine, energy, medical and digital data networks).

For TE Connectivity: Transportation Solutions is the larger, more auto-cyclical segment; Industrial Solutions is the more diversified segment and currently the faster grower on AI-datacentre demand.

What to watch:

  • Relative growth rates -- a shift in revenue mix changes the blended margin and the multiple the market should pay
  • Auto production cycles driving Transportation Solutions more than company-specific execution

transportationEndMarkets.title: Transportation Solutions by end-market
transportationEndMarkets.content:
The three end-markets that make up the Transportation Solutions segment: Automotive (by far the largest), Commercial Transportation (trucks, off-highway) and Sensors.

For TE Connectivity: Automotive revenue tracks global vehicle production and, more importantly, connector content per vehicle as cars add electronics (EVs use roughly 2x the connector content of ICE vehicles) -- that content-growth tailwind is the segment's long-term thesis even when production volumes are flat.

What to watch:

  • Automotive growing faster than global vehicle production (content gains, not just volume)
  • Commercial Transportation and Sensors as smaller, more cyclical swing factors

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For TE Connectivity plc: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For TE Connectivity plc: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For TE Connectivity plc: read it beside CapEx: a business that must reinvest most of its EBITDA is not as cash-generative as the margin suggests.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For TE Connectivity plc: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For TE Connectivity plc: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For TE Connectivity plc: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For TE Connectivity plc: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For TE Connectivity plc: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For TE Connectivity plc: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For TE Connectivity plc: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
